claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl bond coats made from 15–45 μm feedstock have insufficient coating thickness.
The baseline coatings have acceptable but suboptimal as-sprayed oxidation levels.
The proposed intervention is to replace 15–45 μm powder with approximately 45–75 μm powder while leaving all other spray parameters unchanged.
Using 45–75 μm feedstock will increase the deposition efficiency of thermally sprayed FeCoNiCrAl.
The increased deposition efficiency will produce a significantly thicker coating than the 15–45 μm baseline.
The coarser feedstock will preserve microstructural integrity relative to the baseline.
The coarser feedstock will maintain low as-sprayed oxide formation.
Larger powder particles form larger molten droplets.
Droplets produced from larger particles have higher momentum.
Larger particles have a lower surface-area-to-volume ratio.
The larger droplets and higher momentum improve splat formation.
Lower particle surface area relative to volume reduces in-flight oxidation.
The increased mass per particle promotes complete melting under the proposed spray conditions.
Complete melting and robust inter-splat bonding enhance deposition efficiency.
Robust bonding facilitates thicker coating build-up.
The intervention will remain effective under standard thermal-spray and aero-engine bond-coat conditions.
The intervention remains effective only while particle sizes stay within an optimal melting range.
Particles exceeding the optimal melting range may undergo incomplete melting or splashing.
The thickness improvement and oxidation level depend on spray-parameter optimization and the exact particle-size distribution.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies changing particle size without changing any other spray parameters, whereas the boundary and uncertainty fields say that parameters must be adequately tuned or further optimized for the larger particles.

The mechanism presents increased particle mass as promoting complete melting, while the boundary acknowledges that increasing particle size can instead cause incomplete melting; no defined size-dependent melting window reconciles these statements.
